items.title: An element of a valuation ring is a nonzerodivisor on a torsion free module exactly when the module is flat
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the converse companion of the earlier statement that flat modules are torsion free, restricted to valuation rings, and the proof is a 22-line argument with the equational criterion. After quoting the easy direction it assumes the module torsion free and takes an arbitrary relation; renumbering so that one coefficient has minimal valuation it factors all the coefficients through that one, uses torsion freeness to solve for one of the elements, and then exhibits the trivial relations that make the original relation trivial, with the matrix entries written out explicitly. The renumbering and the explicit trivial relation are the substance, and both are displayed.
